boundaries: CI lint step -> golangci-lint (build tags decide which files it reads)
pre-commit gate -> golangci-lint (the same arguments as CI)
integration tests -> Postgres (skipped unless TEST_DATABASE_URL is set)

instruments.evidence: Seven files: the lint tag in ci.yml and in the gate, a tagged known-bad case in the gate's tests, and 30 lint fixes in four integration test files. Boundaries listed in scope.

383b67353 (P1) moved internal/integration's TestDSN change out of P1 because the gate linted the package without the tag; this change is the fix that was deferred. No prior finding on errcheck in the integration tests.

Printed the argument strings the new case compares, extracted from ci.yml and from the gate: both '--timeout=10m --build-tags=integration'; and, with the control applied, CI's became '--timeout=10m' while the gate's did not.

instruments.why: No handler changed; the tests that post multipart uploads still get the same statuses (all 11 upload tests pass against Postgres).

instruments.evidence: The new group comment states the rule in internal/handlers/groups.go:269 ('at least 2 other participants (3 total)'); the request the test keeps sends two others.
One command lives in two places: CI's golangci-lint args and the gate's golangci-lint run. Asked what stops them drifting: nothing did (finding lint-ci-args-unguarded).

instruments.why: No worker or provider contract changed.

instruments.evidence: The tagged fixture carries the same '//go:build integration' line as every file in internal/integration, and sits beside a clean untagged file so the package is lintable without the tag, as internal/integration is not.

Sibling tools that also run without the tag: CI's go vet ./..., staticcheck ./... and deadcode -test ./... in security.yml. With the tag: go vet exit 0, staticcheck exit 0, deadcode output identical to the untagged run. golangci-lint already runs govet and staticcheck with the tag, so nothing is missed today; left unchanged.

TestGroupMemberAdd sent a first create-group request with one other member that the handler always refuses, and never read the response; removed. Every remaining branch in the changed tests is reached (15 tests pass).

The errors that decide a test (multipart writer.Close, part.Write) now fail it with require.NoError; the ones that do not (Close on a finished websocket, RemoveAll of the uploads folder, SetReadDeadline before a read the test tolerates failing) are dropped on purpose with _ =.
The integration tests skip unless TEST_DATABASE_URL is set; a first local run skipped all 16 and printed ok. Re-ran with the variable set to the code's default address: 15 run and pass. CI sets it.
The lint arguments exist twice (ci.yml, the gate); the new case pins them equal.
Searched for other '//go:build integration' files: only internal/integration. Searched the workflows for Go tools without tags: see E1.

instruments.why: No goroutine or shared state changed.

instruments.evidence: The uploads folder is still removed after each upload test (t.Cleanup instead of defer; it runs after the deferred DB close, as before).

The first version of the new case matched CI's arguments as a substring of the gate's command, and its control passed: '--timeout=10m' is a substring of '--timeout=10m --build-tags=integration'. Replaced by an exact comparison in 415a8a185; the control now fails that case alone (11 passed, 1 failed).
The gate is wired: the test's first case asserts frontend/.husky/pre-commit runs it, and it ran on both commits of this change.

Fed the gate a tagged unchecked Close with the tag removed from its command: the new case failed alone (10 passed, 1 failed), then passed with the tag restored. Asked the same of CI's lint step: nothing would notice its tag removed (finding lint-ci-args-unguarded).

golangci-lint --build-tags=integration on the whole backend: 0 issues. go vet -tags=integration and staticcheck -tags integration: exit 0. gofmt: clean. Gate tests: 12 passed. The 15 changed integration tests and the workers DB test pass against Postgres 16.
Both techniques are rows already: C3/G3 found the unguarded CI argument, G1's control found the blind first check. No new instrument.
Ran the real tools, not a reading of the YAML: golangci-lint against the tagged package, and the gate against a known-bad tagged file. No model output involved.

instruments.why: No lazily cached process-wide state changed.

findings.summary: Nothing checked that CI's lint step keeps --build-tags=integration: removing it from ci.yml passed every test and the gate, and CI would again lint none of internal/integration. The first check added for it compared by substring and was blind to exactly that removal.

control.observed: With the tag removed from ci.yml: 'the gate lints with CI's golangci-lint arguments' fails, 11 passed, 1 failed. Against the substring version (76b4daffe) the same patch passed 12 of 12.

instruments.evidence: Pass 2 covers the same seven files plus the exact-comparison rewrite of the new case in 415a8a185.
